classification.difficultyReason: With radii construction explicitly prompted, part b requires choosing four radii, linking base-angle equalities in two isosceles triangles through supplementary angles, and identifying AAS correspondence to prove AB=CD.

content.prompt: In each part, $O$ is the centre of the circle or circles. You will need to construct radii and use congruence in these questions.

spec.description: Circle, horizontal diameter QP and perpendicular vertical chord AB meeting at N; radii OA and OB are intentionally absent.
spec.mathematics: O is the centre, QP is a diameter, N lies on AB and QP, and AB is perpendicular to QP.

answer.short: Construct $OA$ and $OB$. Then $\triangle AON\equiv\triangle BON$ (RHS), giving $AN=BN$; hence $PQ$ bisects $AB$.
answer.worked:
Construct radii $OA$ and $OB$. In triangles $AON$ and $BON$:
$$\begin{align*}OA&=OB &&\text{(radii)}\\ON&=ON &&\text{(common side)}\\\angle ANO&=\angle BNO=90^\circ &&\text{(perpendicular lines)}\end{align*}$$
Therefore $\triangle AON\equiv\triangle BON$ (RHS). Hence $AN=BN$ (matching sides), so $PQ$ bisects $AB$ at $N$.

spec.description: Two concentric circles intersected by one chord line above O, with intersections A, B, C, D in order. No radii or perpendicular are supplied.
spec.mathematics: OA=OD and OB=OC are available only after students construct radii.
spec.answerVisibility: Only circles, chord, centre point and labels are visible.

answer.short: Construct $OA$, $OB$, $OC$ and $OD$. Equal radii and equal base angles give $\triangle ABO\equiv\triangle DCO$ (AAS), so $AB=CD$.
answer.worked:
Construct $OA$, $OB$, $OC$ and $OD$.
$$\begin{align*}OA&=OD &&\text{(radii of the larger circle)}\\\angle OAD&=\angle ADO &&\text{(base angles of isosceles }\triangle AOD\text{)}\\OB&=OC &&\text{(radii of the smaller circle)}\\\angle OBC&=\angle BCO &&\text{(base angles of isosceles }\triangle BOC\text{)}\end{align*}$$
Since $A,B,C,D$ are collinear:
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABO&=180^\circ-\angle OBC\\\angle DCO&=180^\circ-\angle BCO\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle ABO=\angle DCO$. Also $\angle BAO=\angle CDO$, since these are the equal base angles of $\triangle AOD$. Together with $OA=OD$, this gives $\triangle ABO\equiv\triangle DCO$ (AAS). Therefore $AB=CD$ (matching sides).
